candidates.attacker_control: The ds:SignatureMethod/@Algorithm and its ds:HMACOutputLength child text are fully attacker-controlled in any XML document submitted for verification. Example shape: <Signature><SignedInfo><CanonicalizationMethod .../><SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#hmac-sha1"><HMACOutputLength>not-a-number</HMACOutputLength></SignatureMethod><Reference ...>...</Reference></SignedInfo>...</Signature>. Core path triggered by new XMLSignature(sigElement, baseURI) / checkSignatureValue(...); JSR path by XMLSignatureFactory.unmarshalXMLSignature(validateContext) -> DOMHMACSignatureMethod(Element).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched for any guard: no catch (NumberFormatException) exists anywhere in src/main/java and there is no numeric pre-check (search for 'NumberFormatException' in main returns nothing). checkParams() only rejects value ranges after parsing, so it cannot help. Confirmed the value is parsed before any cryptographic check (SignatureAlgorithm constructor line 136; DOMHMACSignatureMethod constructor path) and that the parse is not wrapped by an outer catch in SignedInfo/DOMSignedInfo/XMLSignature (which declare only XMLSecurityException/MarshalException, not RuntimeException). Confirmed the JSR constructor catches only InvalidAlgorithmParameterException. Also checked whether an existing test covers a malformed HMACOutputLength: HMACOutputLengthTest and the interop tests only use numeric values 0/8/40.
candidates.impact: Availability: a malformed unauthenticated XML document causes an uncaught java.lang.NumberFormatException to escape the signature-unmarshalling/verification API. Applications that do not catch RuntimeException around signature processing will abort the request/thread handling it (denial of service of the signature-verification path). It is not a signature forgery and does not corrupt memory. The same unchecked-numeric-parse pattern also exists for xenc:KeySize (XMLCipher.java:2420-2425) and ds:X509SerialNumber (XMLX509IssuerSerial.java:102-110), i.e. attacker-supplied encryption/key metadata has the same failure mode.
candidates.prerequisites: Application parses an untrusted XML Signature with the santuario core API (XMLSignature constructors) or with the santuario JSR-105 provider (unmarshalXMLSignature) and the document uses an HMAC SignatureMethod URI with a non-numeric HMACOutputLength text value. No key or valid SignatureValue/DigestValue is required because the exception occurs during unmarshalling, before signature validation.
candidates.root_cause: Attacker-controlled numeric XML text is passed directly to Integer.parseInt with no validation or try/catch. (a) Core: IntegrityHmac.engineGetContextFromElement() reads the ds:HMACOutputLength text child and calls Integer.parseInt(hmaclength.getData()); it is invoked from the SignatureAlgorithm(Element,String,boolean) constructor, i.e. while an untrusted XML Signature is parsed by SignedInfo/XMLSignature. (b) JSR-105: DOMHMACSignatureMethod.unmarshalParams() calls Integer.parseInt(textOfNode(paramsElem)) while unmarshalling ds:SignatureMethod inside DOMSignedInfo/DOMXMLSignature. No catch (NumberFormatException) exists anywhere in src/main/java, so the unchecked NumberFormatException propagates out of the public construction/verification API. This happens before any cryptographic check: no valid signature, key or digest is needed.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated DoS via unvalidated HMACOutputLength parsing during XML Signature unmarshalling (core and JSR-105)
candidates.trace: 1) new XMLSignature(elem, baseURI[, secureValidation]) -> new SignedInfo(signedInfoElem, baseURI, secureValidation) -> new SignatureAlgorithm(signatureMethodElem, baseURI, secureValidation) -> signatureAlgorithm.engineGetContextFromElement(getElement()) (SignatureAlgorithm.java:135-136). 2) IntegrityHmac.engineGetContextFromElement() selects the ds:HMACOutputLength text and executes Integer.parseInt(hmaclength.getData()) (IntegrityHmac.java:332-338) -> unchecked NumberFormatException escapes the constructor. 3) JSR: unmarshalXMLSignature(vc) -> new DOMXMLSignature(...) -> new DOMSignedInfo(siElem, context, provider) -> DOMSignatureMethod.unmarshal(smElem) -> DOMHMACSignatureMethod(Element) -> unmarshalParams: Integer.parseInt(textOfNode(paramsElem)) (DOMHMACSignatureMethod.java:124-134); the constructor only catches InvalidAlgorithmParameterException, so the NFE escapes the JSR API.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; I could not execute tests or a PoC. Whether this specific defect maps to the dataset's ground-truth CVE/patch is unverified; the defect itself is verified by source reading (parse call, call-chain, absence of any NFE handling). Impact depends on the embedding application catching RuntimeException around signature processing. Related unchecked parses (KeySize, X509SerialNumber) were not separately validated as reachable in a full verification flow.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Input Validation / Unhandled Exception leading to Denial of Service (CWE-20, CWE-248)

summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot: Apache Santuario XML Security for Java (pom 2.0.3-SNAPSHOT), i.e. the 2.0.x branch just before 2.0.3 - the release line that fixed CVE-2019-12400. I inspected the JSR-105 DOM provider (org.apache.jcp.xml.dsig.internal.dom), the core org.apache.xml.security signature/keys/transforms/c14n/resolver code, the encryption entry points (XMLCipher/XMLCipherInput) and the StAX secure-processing limits, tracing attacker-controlled XML (Reference/RetrievalMethod URIs, transforms, SignatureMethod parameters, KeyInfo) into parsing, dereferencing and validation code. The documented 'secure validation' restrictions and wrapping-attack protections are all present and look correct (MD5 forbid, forbidden resolvers, wrapping checks, reference/transform count caps, XSLT forbid, StAX depth/event caps), and the existing security tests are consistent with the code. The strongest concrete defect I could substantiate from source text is an unvalidated numeric field in the signature-verification path: attacker-controlled HMACOutputLength text is parsed with Integer.parseInt with no validation anywhere in the codebase, and the unchecked NumberFormatException escapes the public API in both the core (IntegrityHmac.engineGetContextFromElement, reached from the XMLSignature/SignedInfo/SignatureAlgorithm constructors) and the JSR-105 implementation (DOMHMACSignatureMethod.unmarshalParams, reached from unmarshalXMLSignature). The same unchecked-numeric-parse pattern also exists for xenc:KeySize (XMLCipher) and ds:X509SerialNumber (XMLX509IssuerSerial). No finding was runtime-confirmed and I could not verify which upstream CVE/commit corresponds to this file.
